Flawd 

# Your tests pass. Would they catch a bug?

Coverage says a line ran, not that a bug would be caught. Flawd plants small, realistic bugs in your code and checks whether your suite notices. Every survivor is a blind spot. 

[Start 14-day evaluation](/eval) [See how it works](/flawd#how-it-works) 

$ npm 

 

Interface

## Run it locally. Know where you stand.

Check the strength of your tests with a single command. Everything happens on your machine. 

The live dashboard: score, survivors, and worker activity while a run is in flight.

The HTML report: every mutant with its status, operator, and diff. JSON and SARIF ship alongside it.

Or skip the screenshots: [explore a real report](/flawd/sample-report) — a full flawd run on [go-chi/chi](https://github.com/go-chi/chi): 217 mutants, 34 survivors. 

### Let your agents take it from here.

 $

One command packages every survivor (diff, covering tests, fix guidance) into a handoff file your coding agent reads to write the tests your suite is missing. 

[Try it on your code now](/eval)

Free for 14 days · no credit card required

Why now

## Agents write the tests. Who tests the tests?

AI-generated suites reach high coverage fast, often by matching the structure of the code instead of its meaning. The tests run everything and verify little. Flawd closes the loop: it finds the assertions that aren't there, and `flawd handoff` gives your agent everything it needs to write them. 

 

Mechanism

## Plant a bug. See who notices.

Flawd uses A way to measure test quality: make small changes to a program (mutants) and check that the tests fail. Mutants your suite misses point to untested behavior. [Learn more on Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation_testing) to intentionally inject bugs into your covered lines of code and check whether your tests are sharp enough to catch them. 

It slots into the workflow you already have: one command, your existing suite, run locally or in CI. Nothing to instrument and no pipeline to stand up. The whole loop fits inside a commit.

 

1.  01

    ### Plant

    Flawd parses your code with tree-sitter and plants small, realistic bugs (mutants) only in lines your tests already cover.

2.  02

    ### Test

    Your suite runs against each mutant in an isolated Docker container. A good test fails; that mutant is killed.

3.  03

    ### Report

    Survivors are the point: code that runs under test but is never verified. Each comes with a diff, a risk level, and a category.

4.  04

    ### Hand off

    flawd handoff packages every survivor (diff, source context, covering tests, fix guidance) for your coding agent to write the missing tests.

Capabilities

## Built for real suites, not demos.

### Five languages, one tool

JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust, all parsed with tree-sitter, so there is no per-ecosystem plugin to maintain.

### Coverage-driven

Reads LCOV, Cobertura, or Go coverprofiles and mutates only covered code. No time wasted on lines no test reaches.

### Docker isolation

Every mutant runs in a container: reproducible results, no side effects on your working tree, safe parallelism.

### Incremental by design

SQLite-backed caching between runs, and --diff scopes mutations to the lines changed since any git ref.

### A CI gate that means it

flawd ci --threshold N exits non-zero when the mutation score drops below your bar. Diff-scoped, so it stays fast.

### Reports agents can read

HTML for humans; JSON and SARIF 2.1.0 for pipelines and GitHub Code Scanning; Markdown handoff for coding agents.

Environments

## Runs wherever you need it.

There is no server and no cloud behind Flawd: one binary runs the whole loop, on your machine while you work and in your pipeline when you ship. 

### Local

Made for the inner loop: run it on your dev machine against the code you just changed. Incremental caching and diff scoping keep a run short enough to sit between commits.

Linux

macOS

Windows

### Platforms

One static binary per platform: Linux, macOS, and Windows through WSL2. If your machine runs Docker, it runs Flawd.

### CI

The same binary gates the outer loop: flawd ci scopes mutations to the pull request diff, fails the build below your threshold, and writes SARIF for code review.

Download

## Get the binary.

One self-contained binary per platform — no runtime, no package manager. Downloads are open to everyone; running `flawd run` takes an evaluation or commercial entitlement. 

[macOS Apple Silicon](/download/flawd/darwin/aarch64) [macOS Intel](/download/flawd/darwin/x86_64) [Linux x86\_64](/download/flawd/linux/x86_64) [Linux ARM64](/download/flawd/linux/aarch64) [Linux x86\_64 static (musl)](/download/flawd/linux-musl/x86_64) [Windows x86\_64 Detected](/download/flawd/windows/x86_64) 

### Install

One command — detects your platform, verifies the SHA-256 checksum, and installs to `~/.local/bin`. No sudo. Upgrades are the same command re-run, or `flawd upgrade` once you have it. 

Piping to `sh` deserves suspicion — [read the script](/install) first; it fits on a screen. Prefer to place things yourself? Manual steps: 

macOS

Download with the card above or from the terminal, then mark it executable and put it on your `PATH`. `/usr/local/bin` is system-wide, hence the `sudo`; swap in `~/.local/bin` to skip it. 

Intel Mac? Use `darwin/x86_64` in the URL.

Linux

Same shape; pick your architecture:

`linux/aarch64` for ARM64, or `linux-musl/x86_64` for the fully static build (Alpine, minimal containers). 

Windows

Download the `.exe` with the card above, save it as `flawd.exe` in a folder on your `PATH`, and check it from PowerShell: 

Flawd runs your tests through WSL2 on Windows — install it with `wsl --install` if you haven't. 

Flawd isolates test runs with [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) (Podman and OrbStack work too). Every download redirects to the latest release asset; append `.sha256` to any download URL for its checksum — verify with `shasum -a 256`. Once it's installed, the [docs](https://support.fixture.dev/hc/en-us/categories/53735999402515-Flawd) walk you through your first mutation run. 

Licensing

## Buy once. Keep it.

Every license includes 12 months of updates and support. When that period ends, your current eligible version keeps working. Renew only when you want another year of releases and support.

### Evaluate

**Free** 14 days 

-   The complete product
-   No feature, project, or run limits
-   No credit card
-   One active evaluation machine

 

### Individual

**$149 once** Optional maintenance: $79/year 

-   For one developer who buys and owns the license
-   Unlimited projects and runs
-   Local and CI use included
-   12 months of releases and support
-   Keep eligible releases forever

 

### Team

**$249 per seat once** Optional maintenance: $129 per seat/year 

-   Company-owned, transferable seats
-   One seat for each developer using Flawd
-   Unlimited projects and runs
-   CI runners included
-   12 months of releases and priority-queue support
-   Keep eligible releases forever

 Seats Organization (optional)

1–25 seats. Need more? [Contact us](mailto:support@fixture.dev) for purchasing assistance. 

 

No subscription required. No project, repository, mutant, run, or CI-minute charges. Taxes are calculated at checkout. 

Secure checkout by Stripe. Your license key and activation instructions arrive by email within minutes of purchase. 

Renewing an existing license? [Get your renewal link](/flawd/renew). 

Questions

## The ones we actually get.

### General

How is this different from code coverage?

Coverage tells you a line *ran* under test. It says nothing about whether any assertion checks what that line does. Mutation testing changes the line (flips a comparison, negates a boolean, alters a return value) and sees if any test fails. A survivor is a bug your suite would have shipped. 

Which languages does it support?

JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust, all through tree-sitter parsing. Coverage comes in as LCOV, Cobertura XML, or Go coverprofile, whatever your test runner already produces. 

Do I need Docker?

Yes. Flawd runs your tests inside containers so mutants are isolated and results are reproducible. Docker, Podman, and OrbStack all work. 

Does my code leave my machine?

No. Everything runs locally: mutations are generated and tested on your own hardware. There is no cloud service behind Flawd. 

What about flaky tests?

Flawd detects flaky baselines with configurable retries (`--baseline-retries`), reports error rates separately, and excludes errored mutants from the mutation score, so a flaky suite degrades the report, not the verdict. 

Can I gate CI on it?

That is what `flawd ci` is for: it scopes mutations to the lines changed since your base branch, fails the build below `--threshold`, and writes SARIF for GitHub Code Scanning. 

### Pricing

Is this a subscription?

No. The initial purchase is a perpetual license and includes 12 months of updates and support. Renewal is optional. 

What happens if I do not renew?

Keep using every Flawd release published during your maintenance period. Newer releases and support require renewed maintenance. 

Does CI require another seat?

No. CI runners are included. Buy one Team seat for each developer who uses Flawd. 

Can I use an Individual license for paid work?

Yes, when you personally buy and own it. Employer-paid, reimbursed, or organization-owned use requires a Team license. 

Are there project or usage limits?

No. Flawd runs on your hardware. There are no project, repository, mutant, run, or CI-minute charges. 

Are renewals backdated?

No. Renewing after a lapse starts a fresh 12-month maintenance period on the renewal date. 

Does Team support have an SLA?

No. Team requests enter a priority queue, but support remains best effort. 

Something else? Browse the [docs](https://support.fixture.dev/hc/en-us/categories/53735999402515-Flawd) or [ask us directly](/support) — we answer every message.
